question.text: What is the significance of an FPI's investment being reclassified as Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)?

answer.text: The FPI is automatically granted voting rights proportional to its holding
The FPI gets additional tax benefits on its investments
The FPI and its investor group cannot make further portfolio investment in that company under FPI regulations
The FPI can increase its holding beyond the sectoral cap

explanation.text: The Logic: If an FPI including its investor group breaches the below-10-percent equity threshold and fails to divest the excess holding within five trading days, the entire investment is treated as FDI, and the FPI/investor group shall not make any further portfolio investment in that company under the FPI regulations. The Trap: Reclassification to FDI does not grant new voting or tax benefits and does not allow the FPI to increase its holding beyond applicable sectoral limits — it instead removes the further-portfolio-investment route for that company. Note: The five-trading-day divestment window and the no-further-portfolio-investment consequence are grounded in the checked Series III-A workbook pages.
